names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Νοεμβρίου, «Αγίες Κυριαίνα και Ιουλιανή», with the rank word left off.
Read out of the title on her name link behind the line for 1 ноября ст. ст., «Кириена Тарсийская, мц.», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines it as «Кириены» and gives no by-name.

death.note: Two calendars on two different emperors of one name, and the interval holds both. saint.gr gave «Έζησαν στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Μαξιμιανού (298 μ.Χ.)», which this folder carried as about 298 and which falls in the reign of Maximian Herculius; days.pravoslavie.ru's life sets the arrest «при императоре Максимиане Галерии (305 - 311)», under Maximian Galerius, and its day line prints that reign as the entry's date. Nothing is chosen.

feast.note: Her name page lists this day and no other.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 ноября ст. ст. — «Мцц. Кириены и Иулиании (305-311).»

attestations.note: The line's «Мц.» is martyr, which this folder already held. The name link gives her the by-name «Кириена Тарсийская», of Tarsus, which the folder's English form already carried from the Greek life's words. The life names the governor of Cilicia who arrested the two women Маркиан, the same name the Greek page gives him.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Νοεμβρίου — «Αγίες Κυριαίνα και Ιουλιανή»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry enumerates two women, each with her own heading and her own city, so it is two folders. The corpus holds no Kyriaina at all and the namesweep returned nothing for the name. The English form takes her city because the page gives it: Tarsus of Cilicia. No location is recorded, because Tarsus is where she came from and not where the page puts her death. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (1 October 2026).
